title: Ayaz's sheepskin
hookLine: the king's favorite visits a locked room every day to look at his old sheepskin and shoes (Masnavi 5.1857ff)

lines: A SECRET ROOM, LOCKED EVERY DAY.
cards: Some people keep their first paycheck stub in a drawer. Or the name tag from the diner where they waited tables at sixteen. Or a photo of the tiny apartment with the mattress on the floor.
They've done well since. Once in a while they take it out and look at it. Not to feel bad.
To remember. This week is called guests, and today's story is about a man who kept a secret room. Every day he went in alone and locked the door.
The courtiers were sure he was hiding treasure.

teach.b: Ayaz turns up in more than one of Rumi's stories. He was the beloved servant of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni, a real king remembered in Persian history and poetry.
Ayaz came to court with nothing and became the king's trusted companion.
In Book Five of the Masnavi, Rumi says Ayaz had a little room where he'd hung his old rawhide sandals and his sheepskin jacket, the clothes from his poor days.
Every day he'd go in alone, look at them, and say to himself something like: this is where you came from. Don't get proud.

teach.h: THE COURTIERS DIG AND FIND NOTHING.
teach.b: The courtiers noticed. A locked room, visited every day, in secret. They whispered to the king: he's hiding gold in there, stolen treasure.
The king trusted Ayaz, but he let them look. At midnight they broke in with torches, eager to catch him. And they found a pair of old sandals and a worn sheepskin.
That's all. They couldn't believe it. They dug up the floor.
They drilled holes in the walls. Nothing. They came back to the king pale and ashamed.

There are two ways to hear it. The courtiers are the suspicious mind that assumes everyone is hiding something. And Ayaz, as Rumi reads him, is the soul that remembers its humble origin, not in shame but in gratitude.
Remembering the old shoes made the fine robes less dangerous. Your line: the old shoes.

how: In Persian poetry Ayaz is a model of loyal, humble love, and readers of Rumi take his sandals and sheepskin as a picture of remembering one's origins with gratitude.

o: the poor clothes kept to remember where you came from
a royal robe the sultan gave his trusted servant
a treasure the king's favorite hid in a locked room

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: the king of Ghazni who trusted him

s: the courtiers found stolen gold in the room
they found only old sandals and a sheepskin, dug up the floor, and found nothing more.
Ayaz visited the room to remember where he came from
every day, alone, to keep himself from pride.
Sultan Mahmud was a real king
Mahmud of Ghazni was a historical ruler; Rumi tells more than one story about him and Ayaz.

games.q: you're the king. your courtiers say your trusted friend Ayaz hides treasure in a locked room. what do you do?
o: trust him, but let them look.
games.why: the king trusted Ayaz and let them break in. they found only the old sandals and sheepskin.

practice: Let an old picture of your life come to mind: a first home, a first job, a hard year, the people who got you through it. Look at it the way Ayaz looked at his sandals, not with shame, not with pride, just: this is where I started.
Let some gratitude come if it wants to.

wordCard.voice: Ayaz's sheepskin. The king's favorite visits his old sandals and sheepskin every day, and the courtiers who break in to find treasure find only those. Today's word.

orig.note: Persian: a sheepskin coat, the poor man's jacket Ayaz kept in his room.

carryVoice: Your line: the old shoes. The courtiers looked for gold; Ayaz kept sandals. Day two hundred fifteen, done.
